page.title: Motion — Your body is the controller
page.description: A held body-controlled game prototype for iPhone.

hero.title:
Move.
*Play.*
hero.lede: A held iPhone prototype reads movement on-device and turns it into game input. Camera frames stay on the phone.
hero.note: Held internal prototype. No public TestFlight invite or App Store listing.

screen.alt: Motion Maker running in the internal iPhone build

sections.title: The body is *the controller.*
sections.lede: The iPhone reads pose locally and drives the game. A keyboard debug path exists for the web renderer, not as the product.

screen.alt: Motion Maker enlarged: a score, three hearts, swords and obstacles above an orange ball the player steers by moving

caption.text: The phone tracks the body and renders the game. Only that rendered screen is mirrored to a TV.

sections.title: Camera frames *stay on the phone.*
sections.lede: Vision extracts pose on-device. Screen mirroring sends the rendered game to a TV; Motion does not upload the camera stream.

rows.title: iPhone
rows.body: Reads pose on-device and renders the game.

rows.title: TV
rows.body: Only the rendered game, through the system's own screen mirroring.

rows.title: Motion servers
rows.body: No Motion account and no uploaded camera stream.

aside.title: Motion may fit if
aside.body: you want active, social play on a larger screen without buying a dedicated motion-console system, and you understand that the control loop is unfinished.

aside.title: It is not
aside.body: a public beta, a shipped App Store game, a wearable sensor kit, or a cloud camera service.

items.q: Does video go to a server?
items.a: No. Tracking runs on the iPhone. Mirroring uses the system screen, not our servers.

items.q: Is it on the App Store?
items.a: Not yet. This site will not show Apple’s App Store badge until a live apps.apple.com page exists.
An iPhone. A TV is optional if you already know how to mirror a screen.

closing.title:
Move.
*Keep the camera.*
closing.note: The internal build runs on an iPhone, but physical control feel and fun remain unproven. Work is on hold until one control loop can be tested properly on a real device.

footer.summary: A held iPhone-hosted game prototype: on-device pose tracking turns movement into play, without uploading camera frames.
